content: [{"q":1,"fact":"Jay Dobyns was a University of Arizona football player before joining the ATF in 1987, and had survived being shot on his first day as an agent.","source":"https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-05-me-hells5-story.html"},{"q":2,"fact":"The ATF created a fake charter of the Solo Angeles Nomads, a real Mexican motorcycle club, as the front Dobyns used to approach the Hells Angels.","source":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Black_Biscuit"},{"q":3,"fact":"The operation's undercover activity and arrests were centered in Arizona, coordinated across five states.","source":"https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-05-me-hells5-story.html"},{"q":4,"fact":"I could not verify a specific documented date for the patching ceremony in the available sources.","source":"https://www.google.com/search?q=dobyns+patch+ceremony"},{"q":5,"fact":"No verifiable source was found for an exact verbatim threat quoted during the operation.","source":"https://www.google.com/search?q=dobyns+threat"},{"q":6,"fact":"After the operation, Dobyns's house was burned down in an arson, and he later sued the ATF over how it handled threats against him and his family.","source":"https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-investigations/2014/dobyns-atf.html"},{"q":7,"fact":"The prosecution largely collapsed; many defendants pleaded to far lesser charges than the operation was built around.","source":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Black_Biscuit"},{"q":8,"fact":"Unknown.","source":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Black_Biscuit"},{"q":9,"fact":"There is no documented connection between the Hells Angels and the KKK in the available records.","source":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hells_Angels"}]
